heuristics: H1: the canonical 32-adding walk on the (r-1)/6 automorphism classes has first-collision time approximating the birthday tail 1 - exp(-t^2/(2N)); supported by classical rho analysis, Teske's r-adding-walk experiments, and the toy-scale run in experiment.py (0.42 observed vs 0.4545 ideal at the claimed budget shape); the 1.1*sqrt(N) budget absorbs a >= 14% walk-efficiency loss against the claimed 0.39 lower bound.

Instruction sub-costs are analytical instruction-equivalent bounds (pinned 179-instruction field multiplication; 16-64 instruction bounds for compares, selects and negations), charged at worst case on every step as the cost model permits.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution is claimed or possible.
Single-shot randomized attack with success probability lower bound 0.39 exactly at the protected threshold; no amplification is used and all failures are charged.
The distinguished-point table needs about 2^70.9 bytes; memory is reported and has no score effect.
Automorphism-accelerated rho is standard cryptanalysis, not a novel attack; this is the first qualified bound for this track under the protected cost model.
